document.title: QT4 test catalog format
document.p: A reference for writing the conformance test driver. It covers the W3C QT4 test suite (qt4cg/qt4tests) and gives an outline of the XSLT 4.0 suite (qt4cg/xslt40-test). Both are vendored by tools/update-test-suites.sh into third_party/ at the commits pinned in decision . The authoritative definition is third_party/qt4tests/catalog-schema.xsd together with guide/running.html.

section.title: Files

item.p: catalog.xml: root <catalog test-suite="FOTS" version="4.0"> in namespace http://www.w3.org/2010/09/qt-fots-catalog. It holds global <environment name="..."> elements and <test-set name="..." file="..."/> entries that point to the test-set files.
A test-set file (for example fn/abs.xml) has the root <test-set name>: <description>, <link>, local <environment name>, set-level <dependency> and one or more <test-case>.
<test-case name> holds description, created, modified*, an optional <environment>, <module>*, <dependency>*, <test> and <result>.

<test> holds the expression text, or @file names an external query (rare: encodings, large queries). An XQuery Update test case has several: the ones before the last (@update="true") change the mutable sources, in order, and the last one's result is checked (). Every file attribute is resolved against the base URI of the XML file that contains it.

section.p: Test-set names are prefixed by area: fn-, op-, math-, map-, array-, xs-, prod- (grammar productions), misc-, method- (serialization), app- (use cases), bin- and expath- (EXPath), upd- (Update) and ft- (Full Text).

section.title: Environments
section.p: A test case's <environment> is one of three things:

item.p: ref="name": resolved first in the test-set file, then in catalog.xml.
An inline element with no name and no ref.
Absent, which means an empty static and dynamic context: the context item is absent.

section.p: The environment empty is explicitly empty. Children of an environment:

row.cell: Element
Meaning

XML document. role="." makes it the context item. role="$name" binds an external variable. uri makes it available to fn:doc(uri). A validation attribute (strict, lax) means schema awareness, so skip the test. @dtd, @retain-location (for fn:location) and @mutable (Update) also occur.

cell.code: param name select as source declared

row.cell: External variable. select is an XPath expression, usually a literal or a constructor call. source names a source document. declared="true" means the query prolog already declares it.
The context item, given as an expression.
Text resource for unparsed-text*, json-doc and similar, reached through uri.
Contains source, and query elements. An empty or absent uri means the default collection. query is an XQuery expression whose result forms the collection.
Statically known namespace. An empty prefix sets the default element namespace. Only pure XPath tests use it.

A named or default decimal format for format-number. Properties are decimal-separator, grouping-separator, zero-digit, digit, minus-sign, percent, per-mille, pattern-separator, exponent-separator, infinity and NaN. In 4.0 a property may have the form c:rendition, for example %:pc. Only pure XPath tests use it.
The static base URI. #UNDEFINED means the base URI is absent. If no value is given, the base URI is the URI of the test file.
The test uses this collation URI. default="true" makes it the default collation. Skip the test if the collation is not supported (only codepoint is required).
Schema import. This needs schema awareness, so skip the test.
function-library, sandpit path
XSLT/XQuery function library. gives a writable copy of a directory (EXPath File).

section.p: The <module uri file location> element in a test case maps import module (with an optional location hint) to a file. It is XQuery-only.

section.title: Dependencies
section.p: <dependency type value satisfied="true|false"> can appear on a test set and on a test case. With satisfied="false", the test runs only when the dependency is not satisfied.

The spec type takes space-separated tokens such as XP40+ XQ40+. A token matches if its language is right (XP or XQ, and XT in a few tests) and its version is equal, or, for a token with a trailing +, the version is equal or later. The test runs if any token matches.

item.p: A test-case spec replaces the test-set one. Under AND semantics 13 tests could never run (e.g. set XQ10+, case XP30+ XQ30+).
No spec anywhere means every version of both languages ( cases, mainly in fn-, op- and prod-).
A run targets exactly one language and version: XP40 or XQ40.

section.p: Other types (each value is described in dependency_meanings.xml):

item.p: feature: higherOrderFunctions, schemaImport, schemaValidation, typedData, staticTyping, , namespace-axis, xpath-1.0-compatibility, moduleImport, fn-load-xquery-module, fn-transform-XSLT, fn-transform-XSLT30, infoset-dtd, simple-uca-fallback, advanced-uca-fallback, non_unicode_codepoint_collation, collection-stability, directory-as-collection-uri, non_empty_sequence_collection, olson-timezone, arbitraryPrecisionDecimal, dtd-validation-option, xinclude-option, remote_http, fn-invisible-xml, fn-format-integer-CLDR, schema-location-hint, XQUpdate, fullText*, binary and expath-file.

xml-version (1.0, 1.1, 1.0:4-, 1.0:5+), xsd-version, language and default-language (en, de, ...), , format-integer-sequence, (big_integer, year_lt_0), unicode-version, unicode-normalization-form and .

section.title: Result assertions
section.p: <result> contains exactly one assertion. $result stands for the value of the test expression. The expected values are themselves XPath expressions, unless the description below says otherwise.

row.cell: Assertion
Passes when
The result is one atomic value, eq the expected expression. Numeric promotion and untypedAtomic casting apply.
deep-equal($result, expected).
Some permutation of the result is deep-equal to the expected value. NaN equals NaN.
assert-true / assert-false
The result is exactly xs:boolean true or false, not an effective boolean value.
The result is ().
The result has N items. N is an integer literal.
$result instance of T. The content is a SequenceType.
The effective boolean value of the content expression is true, with $result bound.
string-join($result ! string(), " ") equals the literal text content. With normalize-space="true", both sides are normalized.

The result, serialized (method=xml, indent=no, no XML declaration), matches the literal XML fragment, or the one in @file. Compare canonically or with deep-equal after wrapping in an element. With ignore-prefixes="true", prefixes are ignored.
The result, serialized with the query's own parameters, matches a regex (@flags, unanchored). The regex is literal text or @file.
Evaluation succeeds and serialization fails.
Evaluation raises an error. code is an NCName in the err namespace, Q{uri}local, or *. A different code is usually reported as "pass, wrong error".
all-of / any-of
Every child or at least one child passes. These are used to allow implementation-dependent outcomes, often a value or an error.
The child assertion fails.

section.p: Frequency: assert-true ; error ; assert-eq ; assert-string-value ; assert-deep-eq ; assert-false ; assert-xml ; assert ; any-of ; all-of ; assert-type ; assert-empty ; serialization-matches ; others under 300.

item.p: test sets with test cases. XQ40: cases in sets. XP40: cases in sets.
Both XP40 and XQ40: . XQ40 only: . XP40 only: . Neither (1.0, 3.0 or 3.1 only): .
Every prod-TryCatchExpr test is XQ-only. In the suite, try/catch is XQuery-only.

section.title: xslt40-test layout
section.p: Read by sxml-xslt-test (tests/xslt/driver/, ), which this section describes as it reads the suite.

item.p: catalog.xml is in namespace http://www.w3.org/2012/10/xslt-test-catalog. It holds only <test-set name file> entries: active ones ( more are commented out), with test cases in all, and no environments ("at present there are no global environments", catalog-schema.xsd). of them apply to XSLT 4.0 (tokens XSLT10+ up to XSLT40+, or XSLT40; cases have no spec at all and apply to every version).

tests/<group>/<area>/_<area>-test-set.xml sits next to its .xsl and .xml files. The groups, with case counts: misc , strm (streaming) , insn , attr , decl , fn , type and expr . sandp holds generated streamability-posture tests, none of them in the catalog today.

Scope (): of the , the outside strm and sandp that need none of the features schema_aware, streaming, dtd, XML_1.1, XSD_1.1, backwards_compatibility, HTML4, ICU_spellout. A case that asks for one of them to be absent (satisfied="false") stays in scope.

Dependencies sit inside a <dependencies> wrapper of the test set or the test case. Each child is one dependency, its element name the type: <spec value>, <feature value [satisfied]> and implementation-defined items such as year_component_values, combinations_for_numbering, package_version_resolution, on-multiple-match and maximum_number_of_decimal_digits. Their values are phrases ("support negative year", "CIRCLED DIGIT ONE"), not token lists; only spec values are space-separated tokens. A test-case spec replaces the test-set spec. XPath_3.1 is XSLT 3.0's optional support of XPath 3.1, not a request for 3.1 behaviour.

Environments are named in the test set (<environment name>), referred to by <environment ref> in a test case, or inline there. They hold the QT4 children source, param, , , , , context-item, plus , and output. A source gives its document by file or inline in a <content> child (CDATA), may select the global context item within it (role "."), and has the flags streaming, dtd, defines-stylesheet (the document's xml-stylesheet processing instruction names the stylesheet: cases), and xml-version.

<test> holds package*, stylesheet* (file, role principal or secondary; packages also uri, the package name, and package-version), posture-and-sweep?, param* (name an xs:QName, select, as, static="yes"), then one of initial-template name? (absent name: xsl:initial-template), initial-mode name select? (#default, #unnamed or a QName; select is the initial match selection) and initial-function name, each with its own param children (tunnel for templates and modes, by position for functions), and output (serialize, , well-formed, file, result-var). Without an initial element the stylesheet is applied to the global context item in the default mode. The principal module is the first non-secondary module of <test>, else of the environment ( cases have it in the test, only in the environment). Counts: initial-template , initial-mode , initial-function ; tests use packages.

The assertions are the QT4 set plus assert-result-document uri, assert-message, assert-warning, assert-serialization (method, file), serialization-matches (flags), assert-serialization-error code and assert-posture-and-sweep. assert is evaluated with the document node of the principal result as the context item and the default element namespace none (not with $result); assert-message and assert-result-document each hold one assertion about one message or result document. Counts, as assertions (test cases): assert (), assert-xml (), error (), all-of , serialization-matches (), assert-string-value , assert-result-document (), assert-serialization , assert-message (), assert-warning ; assert-posture-and-sweep occurs only in sandp.
admin/catalog-schema.xsd defines the format. runner/ holds an XSLT-based reference runner.

section.title: XSTS layout (the W3C XSD test suite)
section.p: Read by sxml-xsd-test (tests/xsd/driver/, ), which this section describes as it reads the suite (third_party/xsdtests, ).

item.p: Every element is in namespace http://www.w3.org/XML/2004/xml-schema-test-suite/, every reference an xlink:href (http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink) relative to its file. common/xsts.xsd defines the format.

suite.xml is a testSuite of 93 testSetRefs (two more, the precisionDecimal sets, are commented out and listed in extra-suite.xml). The first, common/introspection.testSet, validates the suite's own files against common/xsts.xsd; it is run since the driver serves the XLink schema document xsts.xsd imports (third_party/w3c-xlink, ; left it out).

A testSet (name, contributor, version?) holds testGroups (name, version?), each with at most one schemaTest and any number of instanceTests (name, version?). A schema test lists its schemaDocuments (loaded one by one, in order, into one schema; valid means it compiles); an instance test has one instanceDocument, validated against the schema of its group's schema test, or against the built-in components alone when the group has none (55 groups). Each test has expected validity version? elements and a current status (submitted, accepted, stable, queried, disputed-test, disputed-spec). testSet/@name repeats across contributors (Assert, CTA, TargetNS, VC, Zone), so the driver names a set after its file: saxonMeta/Assert.testSet is saxon-Assert; a test is GROUP/TEST.

Version tokens (xsts.xsd, version-info): on testSet, testGroup and tests they are or-ed per element ("supports any of them"), on expected and-ed. Tokens fall into classes (XSD version, 1.0 edition, XML substrate, Unicode version, CTR-all behaviour, XPath in CTA, XDM filtering). In the suite: 1.1 times, 1.0 , full-xpath-in-CTA , restricted-xpath-in-CTA , Unicode_4.0.0 , Unicode_6.0.0 ; no other token occurs.

Counts: 41,643 tests in the 92 test sets besides the introspection one (92 more there); statuses accepted 40,635, stable 850, queried 57, submitted 12, disputed-spec 5, disputed-test 1; expected elements valid 26,515, invalid 15,312, indeterminate 16. In scope for an XSD 1.1 processor (each level's version applies, status not queried or disputed, valid or invalid expected): 41,518 (15,329 schema tests, 26,189 instance tests). counted 41,538 by or-ing the three levels' tokens together; applies each level, as xsts.xsd says, which leaves out 19 XSD 1.0 instance tests of wgMeta/substitution-groups.testSet (five of them name files that do not exist) and one 1.0 test group of Saxonica.
